options.label: Psychopathology, Development and Health
options.concept: Study mental health, psychological assessment and development across the lifespan. Explore the biological basis of behavior through neuroscience and use research methods and epidemiology to evaluate health evidence. A youth resilience project examines one approach to prevention.

options.label: Social Influence, Motivation and Organisational Psychology
options.concept: Study how people make decisions, respond to persuasion and work in groups. Combine organizational psychology and behavioral economics with research methods. Examine how television and digital media represent identity and social power.

analysis: The closest programme combines developmental, clinical and health psychology with cognition and empirical methods. Clinical assessment includes interviewing, but lacks the dedicated supervised conversation sequence. The organizational programme shifts exactly 30 EC to organization, behavioral decisions, persuasion and critical media, preserving its focus after the three-course rotation. The proposed programme does not duplicate VU personnel assessment. The genes direction has credible molecular and medical genetics material and a real complementary cognitive course, Psycholinguistics. These do not give the sustained study of heritability and gene-environment effects on behavior that defines the proposed direction. The two interview and experimental brain measurement candidates have valuable partial coverage, including clinical interviewing and neuroscience research design, but insufficient depth for a distinct third programme.

alignment.rationale: Professional psychological conversation skills have no sufficiently direct counterpart in rhetoric or general presentation.
VU requires a dedicated professional conversation skills course. UCR includes interviewing in clinical assessment and qualitative research.
Both introduce psychological theories and brain–behaviour questions; the gateway is narrower than VU’s general introduction.
Shared scientific study of social influences on thought, feeling and behaviour; scope and EC differ.
Lifespan development directly addresses the developmental part of this integrated development/psychopathology unit; disorder depth differs.
Development and organisational courses discuss personality in context; no scheduled course provides the dedicated personality-theory/research unit.
Neurobiology directly addresses the biological-neuroscience part; it does not reproduce the integrated cognitive/biological unit in full.
Sensory/perceptual and action mechanisms are an identifiable neuropsychological subdomain; clinical assessment/lesion breadth is narrower.
Emotion, attention, decisions and higher-order cognitive processes overlap directly with Cognition and Emotion; exact scope and assessment differ.
The selected Addiction unit has no sufficiently specific scheduled counterpart.
The broad cognitive-neuroscience courses are already assigned to their strongest components; no additional full preminor course is inferred.
Molecular biology and lifespan environmental influences do not establish behavioural-genetic interaction methods.
Study design, sampling, experiments/surveys and a research project provide a direct introductory research-method relationship; not identical disciplinary coverage.
Both teach regression and analysis of variance. UCR also covers other multivariate methods.
Data cleaning, manipulation and analysis are an important shared data-method function; psychological applications and scale differ.
Introductory statistics contributes within the UCR methods course already paired above; no second standalone UCR statistics unit is assigned here.
VU combines empirical team research, regression/power, AI literacy, open science and ethics. Qualitative methods or research synthesis do not establish that complete method sequence.
No dedicated psychometric measurement course is scheduled.
Factor analysis as a general statistical method and clinical assessment do not establish test validity/bias/item-response psychometrics.
Machine learning and meta-analysis contribute methods but no sufficiently specific track-statistics counterpart is established.
VU requires a 12 EC individual thesis after completion of all first-year components.
Philosophy of mind directly examines mind/body, consciousness and identity; VU’s broader philosophy/psychology framing is not reproduced in full.
Both study motivation, leadership, groups and organisational behaviour; the UCR course is not a complete organisational-psychology major.
Both cover psychological interventions. VU includes practice in specific low-intensity techniques and digital delivery.
Students choose 30 EC of approved electives or a minor.
